package_info.why_malicious: The package was compromised via a supply chain attack after a maintainer's npm account was phished, allowing an attacker to upload a malicious version containing wallet-draining JavaScript. This code, when loaded by dApps, enabled theft of user cryptocurrency assets by exfiltrating wallet credentials and draining tokens from connected wallets.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when dApp loads connect-kit in browser)
execution_context.file_location: dist/ledger-connect-kit.js (main JavaScript payload loaded from CDN or npm package)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code hooks into the dApp frontend, requests wallet access from the user, exfiltrates wallet addresses and credentials to a remote attacker-controlled server, and initiates unauthorized token transfers, resulting in theft of user assets.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code surreptitiously exfiltrates sensitive wallet information and initiates unauthorized transactions without user consent, which is a hallmark of wallet-draining malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal connect-kit code should only facilitate secure wallet connections and never transmit private wallet data or initiate transactions without explicit user action. The malicious code violates this by sending sensitive data to an external server and draining assets.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate wallet connectors may request account access, but never exfiltrate credentials or automate token transfers to unknown addresses.
key_indicators: Network requests to untrusted external domains
Automated wallet access and token transfer logic
Code present only in compromised package version

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains access to Ledger developer's npm account via phishing.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to publish malicious package version

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is injected into Ledger Connect Kit and published to npm as a new version.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is distributed to downstream projects

attack_chain.action: Downstream dApps and projects load the compromised connect-kit JavaScript from npm or CDN.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code executes in user browsers

attack_chain.action: Malicious JavaScript executes in the browser, requests wallet access, exfiltrates credentials, and initiates unauthorized token transfers.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code in wallet connectors making network requests to untrusted domains
Automated wallet access requests followed by immediate outbound POST requests
Token transfer logic triggered without explicit user action
file_indicators: dist/ledger-connect-kit.js with obfuscated or unfamiliar code
Presence of new or modified JavaScript files in package versions not matching official source
References to external domains in code
network_indicators: Outbound POST requests to domains not associated with Ledger (e.g., malicious-drainer.com, webhook.site, etc.)
Unusual traffic from dApp frontends to unknown endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for JavaScript wallet connector packages that make network requests to untrusted or previously unseen domains, especially immediately after requesting wallet access. Use static and dynamic analysis to flag code that exfiltrates wallet addresses or initiates token transfers without user interaction. Compare package contents and hashes between trusted and newly published versions to detect unauthorized code changes.
